To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
EGP‐2 is a protein of 38 kDa that is expressed by a variety of epithelial tumors, including carcinomas of the breast, colon, lung, ovary, pancreas and prostate.
the SCLC‐cluster 2 antibodies recognize the EGP‐2 antigen, a 38 kDa epithelium‐ associated membrane glycoprotein, encoded by the GA 733‐2 gene.
the GA733‐gene‐encoded proteins are useful markers for epithelial tumors and their metastases and that they are promising targets for immunotherapeutic approaches.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the epitope recognized by a monoclonal antibody, designated Ks1‐4, and its application in the diagnosis and prognosis of human malignancies.

the characterization of the EGP‐2 gene product and its expression in normal and neoplastic tissues, and the development of monoclonal and polyclonal EGP‐2 antibodies as reagents for diagnostic and prognostic purposes.
the identification of tumor antigens and the characterization of their expression in normal and malignant tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EGP‐2 antibodies recognize a glycoprotein encoded by the GA 733‐2 gene.
the EGP‐2 antigen is a 40 kDa glycoprotein, which is a member of the carcinoembryonic antigen gene family.
EGP‐2 and EGP‐1 are both epithelium‐related glycoproteins, which are encoded by two separate genes, GA733‐2 and GA733‐1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SCLC‐cluster 2 antibodies detect the GA733‐ 2 gene product EGP‐2, and the antibodies of the SCLC cluster‐13 group recognize the GA733‐l gene product EGP-1.
the EGP‐2 antigen is expressed by most epithelium‐derived tumors, but not by normal tissues.
EGP‐1 and EGP‐2 are both useful markers for detection of epithelial tumors, but that they do not seem to be of any value for detection of small cell lung cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EGP‐2 protein is not restricted to small cell lung cancer, and that the antibodies are useful tools for detection of a wide range of epithelial malignancies.
EGP‐2 is a useful marker of epithelial differentiation and a potential target for immunotherapy of carcinomas.
SCLC‐cluster 2 antibodies detect EGP‐2, a protein encoded by GA733‐2, a member of a family of closely related genes.
